texts.facts: The present Dar (detailed accident report) arises out of a road road accident that occurred on 09.02.2023, resulting in simple injury to the victim/claimant Poonam Devi. 2. The brief facts of the case are that on 29.09.2022 at about 01:00 p.m. Poonam Devi was going from Tara apartment towards Tuglakabad Extention. She was taken to AIIMS trauma center where she received treatment. 3. An FIR no.0102/2023 was registered u/s 279/337 of IPC against respondent no.1. Upon investigation chargesheet was filed u/s 279/337/201 IPC and 146/196/192 of MV Act before concerned criminal court and DAR was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver cum owner of the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle was not insured with any insurance company. 5. Despite opportunity respondent/driver cum owner neither appeared nor filed any reply or written statement. Sicne there is no defence raised by the respondent, there is no technical requirement of even framing of issues in as much as the fact of accident occurring due to rash and negligent driving has not been disputed by way of a reply.

As regards the quantum of compensation and the respondent who is liable to pay the same, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and MACT No: 1189/2024 Poonam Devi vs. Deepak Kumar P.No. 4 of 14 ss his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of MACT No: 1189/2024 Poonam Devi vs. Deepak Kumar P.No. 5 of 14 ss permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 20.
